title: "database is locked" migrating to 2.0
body:
### What happened?

I get this error message when trying to migrate to RC24
2025-08-09 23:11:20 INF syncthing v2.0.0-rc.24 "Hafnium Hornet" (go1.24.6 linux-amd64) docker@<redacted-host> 2025-08-07 09:47:50 UTC [noupgrade] (log.pkg=main)
2025-08-09 23:11:25 ERR Failed to migrate old-style database (error="openbase: runscripts: database is locked" log.pkg=main)
2025-08-09 23:11:25 INF Syncthing exited (error="exit status 1" log.pkg=main)

comments.author: reporter
comments.body:
Hi, when I mentioned "another method" it was because I couldn't remember the Docker name for storage that are not docker volumes. I searched for the right term: by "another method" I wanted to say "bind mounts"
So, I'm not sure what the original problem preventing the DB migration to v2, but I had the idea to:
1/ create docker volumes for syncthing config files
2/ copy the existing (from v1.30) config files from my bind mount to my new docker volume. 
3/ pointed out in docker compose my syncthing container to that new docker volume
4/ changed in docker compose the syncthing container to v2, run it...
5/ and the migration occurred fine, and all my settings were preserved

Hope this clarifies

comments.author: participant1

comments.author: participant4
comments.body:
Ok thanks @participant1  for the answer.
Yesterday I managed to move my database locally to where Syncthing runs. 
And I changed the Samba-mounted folder to be available in a different location inside Syncthing container, here's my docker-compose snippet:

```
services:
  syncthing:
    image: syncthing/syncthing:2.0.3
    network_mode: host
    volumes:
      - syncthing_storage_local:/var/syncthing/config
      - photos_nas:/tosync

volumes:
  # LOCAL VOLUMES
  syncthing_storage_local:
    driver: local
    driver_opts:
      type: none
      device: /home/<user>/syncthing-config
      o: bind

  # REMOTE VOLUMES
  photos_nas:
    driver: local
    driver_opts:
      type: cifs
      device: "//192.168.1.123/photos"
      o: "username=xxxx,password=xxxx,uid=1000,gid=1000"
```

I think it would be useful to have such type of examples at

https://github.com/syncthing/syncthing/blob/main/README-Docker.md

I can open a basic PR with such snippet if you think it's a good addition...

I also store data on network storage（freeNAS）. This used to work for me：
```
    environment:
      - TZ=Asia/Shanghai
      - STHOMEDIR=/var/syncthing/config
      - HOME=/data
      - PUID=499
      - PGID=499
 ```


GPT told me: 
```
If your Syncthing container’s configuration directory is mounted on a network drive (such as SMB/CIFS/NFS), please check the mount options:
For SMB mounts, add: nounix,vers=3.0,cache=none,actimeo=0
For NFS mounts, enable nolock (in some cases, the opposite—removing nolock—is required)
SQLite will definitely fail on file systems that do not support POSIX locks.
```

Didn't solve my problem，"database is still locked" , Until I did this: 

```
-PUID=1000
-GUID=1000
```
